funnel.note: Everyone the NDH lists as practising in this state.
Without a role there is no organization, so no path to an endpoint at any confidence. This is the binding constraint.

funnel.step: Role names an organization that resolves
funnel.note: The reference points at an Organization that exists.
An organization NPI is what lets the org be joined to any other federal or vendor source.
The site the patient actually visited. No NDH Location carries an endpoint or a parent, so the place layer stops here.

Of these, 6,555 are deterministic (the NDH, or a vendor NPI on a URL listing 10 or fewer). Includes 14,656 reachable only after the vendor-published NPI fill (10,008 of them only through a URL whose vendor lists more than 10 NPIs, which is not deterministic), 26,173 only after name or brand resolution, and 8,076 only via the practitioner's CMS-enrolled group, of which 595 carry no PractitionerRole at all. The NDH alone reaches 1,907.

An endpoint is published against an organization name that matches, but nothing deterministic connects them. This is where the large health systems land: the vendor names the brand, the NDH holds the practitioners under separate legal entities, and the NDH carries no hierarchy to bridge them. Triage material, not a directory linkage.

funnel.step: Endpoint attributed to an EHR vendor
funnel.note: The vendor is derived from the endpoint host and cross-checked against the file that published the URL.

confidence.note: Bands describe method, not quality. Green means the NDH itself carries the whole chain. Yellow means the last link came from a vendor-published NPI that matches an NDH organization: deterministic, but not the directory's own statement. Vendor list means the vendor publishes the organization's NPI beside a URL together with more than 10 other NPIs (a practice-wide or brand-wide list), so the NPI is published but the URL is not shown to serve that organization: counted as reaching an endpoint, not as deterministic. Resolved means the organization was matched to a vendor brand by curated alias, name or brand prefix plus state (H53). Enrolled means only the practitioner's CMS-enrolled group reaches an endpoint. Red means the practitioner reaches an organization and stops. None means no organization at all. Candidate is weaker than red on evidence and is never counted as connectivity: an endpoint exists under a matching name, with nothing deterministic tying it to this organization.

geo.note: County assignment is by the practitioner's postal code, because a postal code is the only geography every practitioner has: only those with a role reach a Location, and Location is where the NDH's coordinates live. Colour encodes rates, never counts, so the map does not simply redraw population.

county_assignment.method: dominant population share, Census ZCTA-county relationship file

systems.note: Health systems, best evidence first. `cms-ownership` groups come from CMS enrollment ownership data, which states ownership and names holding companies explicitly, but covers hospitals only. `nppes-parent` groups come from NPPES is_organization_subpart plus parent_organization_lbn: real, but sparse, sometimes stale, and sometimes a program rather than an owner. `brand-name` groups are inferred from the organization name and cover the rest. The directory's own OrganizationAffiliation resource was tried and rejected: see affiliation_graph below. Since FHI-73 each system's reach is reported per tier and per distinct clinician; see tiers and corrections.

affiliation_graph.note: OrganizationAffiliation carries no `code`, so an edge does not state what the relationship is. The hubs below show the resource is dominated by retail pharmacy corporate structure, so connected components are not health systems and are not used as such.

tiers.note: Each system's reach is counted per distinct clinician at the strongest tier among the member organizations they hold roles at. ndh: the NDH attributes the endpoint to the member. vendor-npi: an EHR vendor publishes the member's NPI beside the endpoint, on a URL listing 10 or fewer NPIs. Both are deterministic. vendor-npi-list: the vendor publishes the member's NPI beside a URL listing more than 10 NPIs, a practice-wide or brand-wide list (athenahealth attaches one practice list to every department), so the URL is not shown to serve that member; inference. alias: a curated, sourced legal-name-to-brand link (analysis/org_aliases.json). name-state and brand-state: the member's name or brand prefix matches a vendor brand in the same state (H53). Those three are inference. cms-enrollment-own-endpoint: the clinician's CMS-enrolled group resolves to an endpoint this system already reaches, or one on the system's own domain; enrollment that lands on another system's endpoint is not counted for this one. systems_reaching_an_endpoint and practitioners_in_a_system_that_reaches_an_endpoint count every tier; the _deterministic keys count the NDH and vendor-npi tiers only.

corrections.what: The health-systems table reported endpoints only through the NDH and vendor-published NPIs, while the practitioner funnel on the same page also counted name and brand resolution and CMS enrollment. Geisinger, St. Luke's, WellSpan and other systems showed zero endpoints although the funnel counted their clinicians reaching the system's own endpoint. Reach is now reported per tier.
corrections.since: 2026-08-16 (26a6208), when the system rollup was added; #169 (2026-10-13) rebuilt the table and kept the omission

corrections.what: The system Practitioners column summed member organizations' practitioner counts, so a clinician with roles at four members counted four times; the six largest PA systems summed to 60,855 against 21,963 distinct clinicians. It now counts distinct clinicians; the old figure is kept as practitioner_org_links.
corrections.since: 2026-08-16 (26a6208), when the system rollup was added

corrections.what: Nine of thirteen curated PA aliases matched no vendor brand because Epic renamed them (MyUPMC, TempleHealth, Thomas Jefferson University Health System), so University of Pittsburgh Physicians and PinnacleHealth resolved to nothing. H51 also kept one NPI per vendor endpoint. The JEFFERSON name group also held organizations that are not Jefferson: on the 2026-10-07 release the Epic brand veto removes two that Epic lists under West Virginia University, and two Jefferson Regional Medical Center units that Epic lists under Allegheny Health Network leave through the CMS hospital ownership path, which groups them before brand grouping runs.
corrections.since: aliases: an unknown date no later than the 2026-10-13 vendor download, which is the first cache checked; one NPI per endpoint: since H51 was published; JEFFERSON merge: since brand grouping (2026-08-16)

corrections.what: A vendor-published NPI was counted as a deterministic link even when the vendor lists that NPI beside a URL together with dozens or hundreds of others: athenahealth attaches one practice-wide list to every department, and Epic brands list up to 1,881. A match through a URL listing more than 10 NPIs is now its own tier, vendor-npi-list, shown as inference. athenahealth's shared base URL, common to all its customers, no longer attributes at all.
corrections.since: the vendor-NPI fill (2026-08-16); the shared athenahealth URL since H51 was published

known_systems_unreached.note: Known systems that publish an endpoint on their own domain which no member organization's route (NDH, vendor NPI, alias, name or brand) connects to their clinicians in this release. Each row says whether CMS enrollment reaches it instead. Measured every run, because a zero here is a measured gap, not a missing lookup.

vendor_brand_vetoes.note: Organizations kept out of a name-inferred brand group because Epic's User-access Brands file lists their NPI under a brand that does not agree with the name. They stay in the ledger as standalone organizations.

systems.routing_caveat: A system reaching an endpoint is not a routing answer. Large systems publish several: UPMC has an Epic endpoint for its physicians and separate athenahealth endpoints for individual surgery centres. Every endpoint found in a system is listed with the member that carries it, and none of them is presented as the one serving a given practitioner.

excluded_third_party.note: Billing, revenue-cycle, management and staffing vendors whose name appears on many unrelated providers' records. They are not grouped into systems and stay in the ledger as standalone organizations. Matched by an explicit list or by a vendor-type name shared across many cities or states.

out_of_state_endpoints_dropped.note: Endpoints a system would have reached only through a member organization recorded in another state. Dropped from the system rollup unless that member is the system itself. Members with no recorded state are kept and counted, because they cannot be shown to be out of state.

limits: Reaching an endpoint is not the same as the endpoint answering. Liveness is measured separately in H1-H5 and is not folded in here, because a reachable-but-dead endpoint should not be counted as connectivity.
The vendor is derived from the endpoint host. That is reliable because vendors host tenants on their own domains, but it is inference and is labelled as such.
Location is counted as named, not as resolved to a site with its own endpoint. No NDH Location carries an endpoint or a parent in this release, so site-level routing cannot be measured yet.
A practitioner with several organizations is counted at the best band any of them reaches. The funnel is per practitioner, not per role.
